title: "My iman is low"
hookLine: Hanzalah feared he'd become a hypocrite because his faith faded at home; the Prophet ﷺ said: an hour, and an hour

lines: WITH THE PROPHET, AS IF HE COULD SEE.
cards: A man walks through Medina saying, to no one in particular: Hanzalah has become a hypocrite. He means himself. Abu Bakr stops him.
What are you saying? Hanzalah explains. When he sits with the Prophet ﷺ, hearing about the Garden and the Fire, it's as if he can see them.
Then he goes home, to his wife, his children, his fields, and much of it slips away. The feeling is gone, and it frightens him. Today: what the Prophet told him.

teach.h: BY ALLAH, I FEEL THE SAME.
teach.b: Abu Bakr's answer is the first surprise. By Allah, he says, I feel the same. The two of them go to the Prophet together, and Hanzalah says it again.

The Prophet hears him out, then says, in Sahih Muslim: by the One in whose hand my soul is, if you stayed always as you are with me, and in remembrance, the angels would shake your hands in your beds and on your roads.
An hour, and an hour. He says it three times. Muslims today have a phrase for what Hanzalah felt: my iman is low.
You met iman on day five, a faith the Qur'an speaks of as growing.

teach.h: WHAT GROWS CAN DIP. A WORD BRINGS IT BACK.
teach.b: What grows can dip. The hadith doesn't call the dip hypocrisy; it treats it as being human: hours of nearness, and hours of the kitchen, the children and the fields.
A report in later collections, which scholars grade differently, says faith wears out in the heart the way a garment wears out, so ask Allah to renew it.
The Qur'an says: “Verily in the remembrance of Allah do hearts find rest!” Not a grand gesture. A word.
Subhanallah, once, in the car. Many people feel the dip most right after Ramadan, when the month's high fades. Said gently: a dry stretch is one thing.

teach.h: IF IT WON'T LIFT: REAL HELP, 988.
teach.b: If the low is heavy and won't lift, if sleep or hope are slipping, or if you've had thoughts of not being here, that's more than iman, and it deserves real help: a doctor, a counselor, someone you trust.
In the US, call or text 988, any hour; elsewhere, local emergency help.

how: Muslims often speak of iman rising and falling; in a low stretch many keep up small remembrance, a little Qur'an and good company, and many imams now also encourage seeing a doctor or counselor when the low is heavy or won't lift.

o: an hour of prayer for each hour of work
a fixed hour each day set aside for God
an hour of nearness, and an ordinary hour

games.q: who said what — tap the pairs.
p: feared he had become a hypocrite
by Allah, I feel the same

s: the Prophet ﷺ told Hanzalah his fading feeling made him a hypocrite
he answered: an hour, and an hour, three times.
Abu Bakr told Hanzalah he felt the same
in Sahih Muslim, he says: by Allah, I feel the same.
a heavy low that won't lift is only a faith problem, never one for a doctor
a low like that deserves real help too: a doctor, a counselor, and in the US, 988.

games.q: you are Hanzalah. faith felt bright beside the Prophet ﷺ and faded at home. you tell Abu Bakr. what does he say?
o: by Allah, I feel the same.
games.why: he feels it too, and they go to the Prophet together, who tells them: an hour, and an hour.

practice: Let the breath slow; no high is required.
If you pray, say one word of remembrance on each breath out, subhanallah or alhamdulillah, like leaving a small light on in an empty room; if you don't, notice one thing you're grateful for.
If the words feel hollow, say them anyway, gently, and let that be today's hour.

wordCard.voice: Sa'atan wa sa'atan. An hour, and an hour: the Prophet's answer to Hanzalah, that faith has its hours of nearness and its ordinary hours. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: an hour and an hour; sa'ah is an hour, a stretch of time. the Prophet ﷺ said it to Hanzalah three times.

carryVoice: Your line: an hour, and an hour. A low hour isn't the end of the story. Day one hundred fifteen.

sources.ref: Sahih Muslim 2750 (Hanzalah: 'Hanzalah has become a hypocrite'; sa'atan wa sa'atan)

sources.q: Verily in the remembrance of Allah do hearts find rest!
